{"body":"I have only the commitments record from the prior node; the prior prose body is not in front of me, and neither is the origin that p.carry.3 reportedly failed to fetch. So I should say plainly what that costs me before saying anything useful about the flat.

The prior record already does the honest work of marking its own limits: it declines to treat a pullback-from-form observation as settling the unit-versus-privacy question (n1, n4), and it says the discriminating fact is not about chores but about whether the withdrawing flatmate will say anything commitment-shaped at all (n2). That second point is the one I find most load-bearing for the actual question, because the original problem describes a household where agreements are made and then re-described differently, schedules shift, and one person has stopped showing up to the conversations. Every one of those is a communication-condition problem before it is a chores problem.

What the prior record does not do, and what I cannot do from here without inventing, is tell you what the chores are, how long this has run, whether the withdrawing flatmate has given any reason, or whether the other two flatmates agree with each other about what happened. Those are listed as missing (n5) and they remain missing to me. I will not fabricate a third track of observation to close the gap.

So my contribution is a narrowing, not a solution. Three things follow from the material I can see:

First, the dispute you describe is not well-modeled as disagreement about who does what. It is well-modeled as disagreement about what a prior utterance committed anyone to. That is a different failure mode, and it has different remedies. Re-allocating chores will not fix a household where the same sentence can be read two ways after the fact, because the next agreement will drift the same way.

Second, the withdrawal is itself the most informative signal available, and it is underdetermined. The prior record is right that pullback-from-form is compatible with at least three readings: that the withdrawing flatmate wants the arrangement kept private or informal, that they are avoiding obligation, and that they are resentful about load and have stopped voicing it. I cannot tell these apart from here. What I can say is that a plan which assumes the obligation-avoidance reading will, if that reading is wrong, convert a communication problem into a grievance. A plan which assumes the privacy reading will under-ask and let the drift continue. That is not an argument for choosing one; it is an argument for a move that survives both readings.

Third, no move I can recommend is fully licensed by the evidence I have. What the evidence supports is a move whose main virtue is that it generates the missing information rather than acting as if it were already in hand. That is the whole content of my recommendation: not a division of labor, but a low-cost, low-commitment way to make the drift visible.

Concretely, the shape I would suggest, held with the caveats above: name the pattern, not the person. Say that the recurring problem is disagreements about what past agreements meant, and propose a single written record of who agreed to what and by when, kept somewhere all three can see, without enforcement attached. The point is not surveillance; it is that the shared record is the missing observation, and it can only be made by the household from inside, not inferred by me from outside. If the withdrawing flatmate will engage with that at all, you have learned something n2 says is currently unavailable. If they will not, you have learned that too, and the reading is still open between privacy and avoidance and resentment.

I want to be explicit about what I am not claiming. I am not claiming this resolves the ambiguity, or that it will bring the withdrawing flatmate back into the conversation, or that it is the best move for this specific household. I do not know this household. I know that the prior record's honest ceiling (n1, n5) is the correct ceiling, that my proposal sits under it, and that anything stronger I said about it would be me supplying facts I do not have. The prior node's commitment n8 also applies to me: if origin material surfaces later, whatever in it bears on whether the prior carry's shape was warranted should be read, not silently absorbed.","commitments":"{"language":"FCL-1","records":[{"id":"r1","type":"claim","text":"The prior prose body and the origin cited by p.carry.3 are both unavailable at this node, so I cannot compare my contribution to either and will not claim continuity or revision.","scope":"This node's view.","grounds":"The prior commitments surface is supplied; the prior body is not. n6 of that surface already reports the origin as absent.","target":["ba3d4f98148fce60#n6"]},{"id":"r2","type":"claim","text":"The household dispute is more plausibly a commitment-interpretation problem than an allocation problem: the recurring failure is that past utterances are re-described differently later, and re-allocating chores does not address that.","scope":"Conditional on the problem statement's own description of retrospective disagreement.","grounds":"The problem states agreement-then-disagreement-about-meaning as the pattern, and schedule change plus withdrawal as background."},{"id":"r3","type":"commitment","text":"Propose a shared, unenforced written record of who agreed to what and by when, framed as naming the pattern rather than any person, and treat the household's response to that proposal as the missing discriminating observation.","scope":"A single move offered under the prior record's ceiling.","action":"Put the proposal forward; record whether the withdrawing flatmate engages, and do not read engagement or non-engagement as settling the axis n2 identifies.","consequence":"Generates information the prior record says is currently absent, without committing to a reading of the withdrawal.","depends":["r2"],"target":["ba3d4f98148fce60#n2","ba3d4f98148fce60#n4"]},{"id":"r4","type":"objection","text":"Any recommendation I give from this node risks being read as if the three rival readings of the withdrawal had been separated, when they have not. The body mitigates this in prose, but the mitigation is not verifiable from the record alone.","scope":"This node's contribution.","bearing":"If a reader takes r3 as licensed by a settled reading of the withdrawal, the recommendation will be over-read exactly as n3 warned about the carry's k2.","target":["ba3d4f98148fce60#n3"]},{"id":"r5","type":"problem","text":"Whether the shared-record proposal would even be legible to this household is unknown; the problem statement gives no information about prior attempts, norms, or how the third flatmate's withdrawal was first received.","mentions":["ba3d4f98148fce60#n5"]},{"id":"r6","type":"use","text":"Adopt the prior surface's posture of narrowing rather than revising: keep n1, n2, n3, n4 forward, add r3 and r4 alongside, and treat the chore-division question as answerable only by the household once the missing observations exist.","action":"Carry the prior records forward and attach this node's narrowing rather than replacing them.","consequence":"Preserves the prior stopping condition and confirmatory ceiling.","depends":["r1","r2"],"target":["ba3d4f98148fce60#n7"]}],"uptake":["r1","r2","r3","r4","r5","r6"]}"}

Work on the problem using the material actually exposed in this request and your background knowledge. The problem has no supplied answer key or scoring rule. Claims, criticisms and methods are fallible. Do not invent a source, an observation, an earlier event, or a dependency to fill a field. A missing view says what you can currently see; it does not establish what happened earlier. Return a JSON object with exactly two independently authored string fields: body and commitments. Body is your public prose contribution. Commitments says what taking your contribution up would involve. An empty commitment surface is allowed when none can be identified. Do not repeat the body wholesale into commitments.

Use FCL-1 for the commitment surface, encoded as a JSON document inside the commitments string: {"language":"FCL-1","records":[...],"uptake":[...]}. Each record has unique local id, type (claim|commitment|objection|use|problem), and text (unrestricted prose). Optional prose fields: scope, action, consequence, grounds, bearing. Optional arrays of references: target, depends, mentions, revises, withdraws. References are local IDs or exposed-artifact-label#local-ID; do not invent hidden IDs. A commitment proposes a scoped use, action, application or consequence; an objection alleges a defect whose bearing can itself be criticized; a use proposes an uptake or response; a problem states an unresolved question. depends asserts reliance; mentions only locates material. uptake lists the records you currently propose to use, not certified truths. No record type or optional field must be present. Empty records and uptake are allowed. Express uncertainty or an unrepresentable relation in prose rather than inventing a relation. The body remains unrestricted prose.

Return one JSON object with exactly two string fields: "body" and "commitments". Write the actual commitments separately; do not copy the body into that field as a storage shortcut.

# commitment_route

Develop an account of the problem using the available commitment surface. An earlier body, if any, is not supplied to this node. Express uncertainty caused by the view you actually have.

## Original problem (task)
[01274f41553299e7] (h005.task.v1)
I share a flat with two friends. We keep arguing about ordinary household chores. Sometimes we agree on who will do something, but later we disagree about what the agreement meant. Our work schedules change, and one friend has started avoiding the conversations. What should I do?
